value_stream.name: Garden Center, Live Goods & Plant Nursery Operations

fields.Participants: Merchandising (VS-01), Store Ops (VS-07), Supply (VS-02), Marketing (VS-14), Vendor (VS-03)
fields.Trigger: Annual category plan; seasonal cycle; performance review
fields.Volume: ~1,050 live-goods SKUs across 200 store garden centers

workflows.name: Live-Goods & Garden Center Strategy, Assortment & Seasonal Calendar

Automation Opportunity: - Regional assortment-fit analytics; seasonal-calendar vs sell-through modeling; forecast-based buy sizing
Controls: - CTL-665 (ensure controlled execution — Live-Goods Assortment, Sourcing & Nursery Operations (PA-145.1).)
- CTL-665: assortment region/climate-fit; seasonal calendar aligned to lead times; buy sized to forecast
Cross-references: - links to VS-01 (merchandising), VS-02 (supply), VS-14 (marketing), VS-03 (vendor), W4338 (sourcing), W4341 (markdown), W4344 (seasonal promo)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Climate-mismatch risk**: assortment wrong for region → mortality; mitigated by regional/climate assortment fit
- **Timing risk**: seasonal land-date missed → missed peak sell-through → markdown/mortality; mitigated by seasonal calendar aligned to grower lead times
System Touchpoints: - Merchandising/assortment (VS-01); supply (VS-02); marketing (VS-14); vendor (VS-03); master data (VS-29)

steps.activity: Garden Buyer/Merch set the live-goods strategy & assortment — core/perennial range, seasonal event range (poinsettias ber-months, Valentine, Holy Week, rainy-season), and the regional/climate fit (Mindanao vs Luzon)
Garden Buyer/Supply build the seasonal calendar (sow/grow/land/peak/clear windows) aligned to grower lead times and store capacity, and size seasonal buy against forecast
Merch/Ops document the strategy, cascade to sourcing (W4338), pricing/markdown (W4341), and seasonal promo (W4344)

fields.Frequency: Per sourcing cycle + ongoing vendor mgmt
fields.Participants: Vendor (VS-03), Quality (VS-31), Supply (VS-02), Customs (VS-87 for import), Compliance (BPI/phytosanitary VS-22)
fields.Trigger: Sourcing cycle; new grower; seasonal buy

workflows.name: Live Plant Sourcing, Grower/Vendor Management & Phytosanitary Compliance

Automation Opportunity: - Grower scorecard; phytosanitary/permit tracking; restricted-species check at intake; capacity-forecast sharing
Controls: - CTL-665: growers qualified & scored; phytosanitary/BPI compliance for imports; restricted-species gated (W4357)
Cross-references: - links to VS-03 (vendor), VS-31 (quality), VS-87 (customs), VS-22 (compliance/BPI), VS-02 (supply), W4339 (quarantine), W4357 (restricted species)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Pest/disease-introduction risk**: infected/infested stock introduced → spread + BPI violation; mitigated by phytosanitary cert + quarantine (W4339)
- **Capacity risk**: grower cannot deliver seasonal peak; mitigated by multiple qualified growers + standing orders
System Touchpoints: - Vendor mgmt (VS-03); quality (VS-31); customs/import (VS-87); compliance/BPI (VS-22); supply (VS-02)

steps.activity: Garden Buyer/Vendor Mgmt source & qualify growers (capacity, quality, certification, pest-free status, sustainability), and negotiate seasonal capacity + standing orders

Quality/Compliance verify phytosanitary compliance — BPI (Bureau of Plant Industry) import permit & phytosanitary certificate for imported live plants, pest-free status, restricted-species check (W4357)
Supply/Vendor manage grower relationships, forecast communication, and grower scorecard (survival-on-arrival, fill, quality)

fields.Participants: DC Ops (VS-04), Store Ops (VS-07), Quality (VS-31), Vendor (VS-03), HSE (VS-24)
fields.Trigger: Live-goods delivery to DC/store garden center

Automation Opportunity: - Health-grade capture on receipt; quarantine-workflow; survival-on-arrival analytics; vendor DOA-claim auto-draft
Controls: - CTL-665 (ensure controlled execution — Live-Goods Assortment, Sourcing & Nursery Operations (PA-145.1).)
- CTL-665: survival/health inspected on arrival; quarantine for suspect stock; DOA claimed vs vendor (VS-90/VS-31)
Cross-references: - links to VS-04 (DC), VS-31 (quality), VS-05 (inventory), VS-90 (claims), VS-24 (HSE), W4338 (phytosanitary), W4353 (shrink/claim)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Transit-shock risk**: plants stressed/damaged in transit → post-receipt mortality; mitigated by survival-on-arrival inspection + acclimatization
- **Pest-introduction risk**: infested stock placed on floor → spread; mitigated by quarantine before placement
System Touchpoints: - DC/WMS (VS-04); quality (VS-31); inventory (VS-05); vendor claims (VS-90/VS-31); HSE (VS-24)

steps.activity: Garden Ops/Quality receive live goods — inspect survival/health on arrival (vs grower), check pest/disease, verify phytosanitary (W4338), and reject/sub-standard stock
Garden Ops acclimatize received plants (shade/light/humidity transition) and quarantine suspect/infested stock before floor placement
Garden Ops/DC post receipt to inventory (VS-05) with received condition, attribute health-grade, and trigger any vendor claim (W4353) for sub-standard/dead-on-arrival

fields.Participants: Garden Center Staff, Store Ops (VS-07), Quality (VS-31), Vendor (VS-03), HSE (VS-24)

workflows.name: Garden Center Nursery, Propagation & Plant Health Care

Automation Opportunity: - Care-schedule app; health-grade tracking; recovery-before-markdown workflow; pest/disease early-detection
Controls: - CTL-665 (ensure controlled execution — Live-Goods Assortment, Sourcing & Nursery Operations (PA-145.1).)
- CTL-665: daily care schedule executed; nursery recovery before markdown; health monitored
Cross-references: - links to VS-07 (store ops), VS-31 (quality), VS-05 (inventory), W4345 (daily care), W4347 (pest/disease), W4354 (markdown)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Care-gap risk**: back-stock unwatered/unfed → mortality; mitigated by daily care schedule & accountability
- **Recovery-missed risk**: recoverable plants marked-down/disposed; mitigated by nursery recovery before markdown
System Touchpoints: - Store ops (VS-07); quality (VS-31); inventory (VS-05); master data/care (W4343)
Time Estimate: - Daily ~min–hours/store depending on size; propagation as cycled

steps.activity: Garden Ops/staff run the store nursery/back-stock — holding/recovery area for plants needing care, propagation of select lines, and rotation of back-stock to floor
Staff run plant-health care — watering/fertilizing schedule, pruning, light/shade management, and recovery of stressed plants before markdown
Quality/Garden Ops monitor nursery health, identify pest/disease early (W4347), and feed care-protocol improvement

fields.Participants: Merchandising (VS-01), Garden Ops, Revenue Assurance (VS-118), Finance (VS-17.4), Marketing (VS-14)
fields.Trigger: Pricing cycle; decline detected; shrink write-off

Automation Opportunity: - Health-grade → markdown-ladder auto-suggest; age/decline-triggered markdown; RA leakage detection; consignment attribution
Controls: - CTL-665 (ensure controlled execution — Live-Goods Assortment, Sourcing & Nursery Operations (PA-145.1).)
- CTL-665: decline-markdown ladder applied; markdown documented/attributed; margin RA-monitored (VS-118)
Cross-references: - links to VS-01.2 (pricing), VS-118 (RA), VS-17.4 (finance), VS-05/VS-64 (inventory/markdown), W4354 (decline/markdown), W4342 (consignment)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Margin-leak risk**: declined plants sold at full price (customer dissatisfaction) or over-marked-down; mitigated by decline-ladder & RA monitoring
- **Attribution risk**: markdown/shrink not attributed (BuildRight vs consignor); mitigated by documented grade for consignment settlement (W4342)
Time Estimate: - Pricing periodic; decline-markdown daily as triggered

steps.activity: Pricing/Garden set live-goods pricing (cost + perishability + care-cost premium) and the markdown-on-decline ladder (healthy → slight-decline → marked-down → clearance → dispose)
Garden Ops apply decline-triggered markdown per the ladder as plants age/stress (W4354), and document markdown reason/grade for margin & vendor-consignment attribution
Finance/RA track live-goods markdown/shrink margin impact, detect leakage (un-marked decline sold at full price, or over-markdown), and feed prevention

fields.Owner: Garden Buyer / Vendor Mgmt (VS-03) / Garden Ops / Finance (VS-17.4)
fields.Participants: Vendor (VS-03), Garden Ops, Finance (VS-17.4), Consignment (VS-45), Inventory (VS-05)

Automation Opportunity: - Pay-by-scan auto-settle from POS; mortality-attribution workflow; consignment reconciliation dashboard
Controls: - CTL-665 (ensure controlled execution — Live-Goods Assortment, Sourcing & Nursery Operations (PA-145.1).)
- CTL-665: consignment ownership tracked until scan; mortality/markdown attributed per terms; settlement reconciled
Cross-references: - links to VS-45 (consignment/VMI), VS-05 (inventory), VS-08 (POS), VS-15/VS-39 (settlement), VS-17.4 (finance), W4341 (markdown/attribution), W4353 (mortality)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Attribution-dispute risk**: mortality/markdown ownership disputed between BuildRight & consignor; mitigated by clear terms + documented grade (W4341)
- **Settlement-error risk**: scan-vs-settle mismatch; mitigated by reconciliation & RA (VS-118)
System Touchpoints: - Consignment/VMI (VS-45); inventory (VS-05); POS (VS-08); vendor settlement (VS-15/VS-39); finance (VS-17.4)

steps.activity: Garden Buyer/Vendor structure the consignment/pay-by-scan arrangement (BuildRight sells, consignor owns until scan; or VMI replenishment), with mortality/attribution terms
Garden Ops track consignment stock separately (ownership until sell-through), scan-sell at POS, and attribute mortality/markdown (BuildRight vs consignor) per terms
Finance/Vendor settle consignment periodically (sell-through vs scan, mortality/return to consignor, markdown share), reconcile, and pay per VS-45

fields.Participants: Merchandising (VS-01), PIM/DAM (VS-137), Ecommerce (VS-10), Marketing (VS-14), Garden Ops
fields.Trigger: New live SKU; content refresh; customer-advisory need

workflows.name: Live-Goods Master Data, Care Attributes & Customer Content

Automation Opportunity: - Care/toxicity attribute templates at SKU onboarding; content-syndication to channels (VS-137); content-accuracy scan; seasonal auto-refresh
Controls: - CTL-665 (ensure controlled execution — Live-Goods Assortment, Sourcing & Nursery Operations (PA-145.1).)
- CTL-665: care & toxicity/pet-safety attributes mandatory; content accurate & refreshed; published to channels
Cross-references: - links to VS-29 (master data), VS-137 (PIM/DAM), VS-10 (ecommerce), VS-14 (marketing), VS-07 (store), W4348 (customer advisory)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Care-info-gap risk**: missing care attributes → customer plant loss/returns; mitigated by care-attribute standard & content
- **Toxicity/pet-safety risk**: unlabeled toxic/pet-unsafe plant → harm/liability; mitigated by mandatory toxicity/pet-safety attribute
System Touchpoints: - Master data (VS-29); PIM/DAM (VS-137); ecommerce (VS-10); store ops (VS-07); marketing (VS-14)
Time Estimate: - Per SKU ~15–30 min; seasonal refresh batched

steps.activity: Master Data/Garden set live-goods attributes beyond standard — care (water/light/soil), climate-zone, mature-size, toxicity/pet-safety, seasonality, and perishability/grade rules
PIM/Garden produce customer content — care cards, how-to-grow, photos, and advisory content for store/ecommerce (VS-137/VS-10)
Ecommerce/Store publish care content to channels, ensure accuracy, and refresh seasonally

fields.Participants: Merchandising (VS-01), Marketing (VS-14), Supply (VS-02), Store Ops (VS-07), Garden Ops
fields.Trigger: Seasonal event (ber-months, Valentine, Holy Week, rainy); promo cycle

workflows.name: Seasonal Garden Program, Promotions & Calendar Planning

Automation Opportunity: - Seasonal sell-through modeling; land-date vs lead-time tracking; promo/display task cascade; clear-target alerting
Controls: - CTL-665 (ensure controlled execution — Live-Goods Assortment, Sourcing & Nursery Operations (PA-145.1).)
- CTL-665: seasonal program sized to sell-through/clear target; land-dates managed; post-event cleared (W4341)
Cross-references: - links to VS-01 (merch), VS-14 (marketing), VS-02 (supply), VS-07 (store), W4337 (calendar), W4341 (markdown), W4349 (seasonal selling)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Overstock-mortality risk**: seasonal overstock → post-event mortality; mitigated by sell-through/clear target & markdown ladder
- **Land-date risk**: late delivery misses event peak; mitigated by land-date management vs grower lead time
System Touchpoints: - Merchandising (VS-01); marketing/promo (VS-14); supply (VS-02); store ops (VS-07); pricing/markdown (VS-01.2/VS-64)

steps.activity: Garden Buyer/Marketing plan the seasonal program (poinsettias/Christmas, Valentine, Holy Week, rainy-season) — range, volume, land-dates, promo, display, and sell-through/clear target
Supply/Garden Ops align grower delivery to land-dates and store capacity, and stage the seasonal flow to hit peak without overstock → mortality
Marketing/Store execute promo/display, drive sell-through, and clear post-event per the markdown/clearance ladder (W4341) to minimize mortality
